dedupe_keys.name: achem software based end to end channel and radio emulator digital twin framework for usrp based wireless systems

description: ACHEM (A Channel Emulator) is described as the first software-based, end-to-end wireless channel emulation environment and toolset for communication systems built on software-defined radios, specifically USRPs. It emulates any USRP-based system at the I/Q level in a purely digital environment, without vehicles, USRPs, FPGAs or GPUs, and supports multiple transmitters and receivers, MIMO, multiple frequencies, heterogeneous sampling rates, real-time node mobility through vehicle emulation, antenna radiation patterns and various channel models. It is validated with GNU Radio, srsRAN 4G/5G and OpenAirInterface. Producer: Anil Gurses and Mihail Sichitiu, submitted to arXiv on 6 April 2026 and to an IEEE journal. Coverage: laboratory emulation, not a geographic area. Access: paper on arXiv; no code repository was read on the abstract page, so an open-source release is not verified. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC-BY-SA-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: only the abstract page was read, and performance and fidelity figures were not checked. Simulation uses: it lets network developers test radio software in a digital twin before field deployment, supporting capacity and coverage studies. Related records: none linked.
